tasks.short: Interpret boiler blueprints for part relationships and dimensions

steps.what: Study blueprints to determine part locations, relationships and dimensions

tasks.design: Keep blueprint interpretation with the boilermaker using the released drawing in {DOCS}. Existing drawing zoom, layers and measurements can support inspection, but they do not remove the need to understand dimensions and assembly relationships.
tasks.previous_blocker: A dimension has to be interpreted in the correct drawing and assembly context.
tasks.enabler_now: No demonstrated tool removes the required interpretation time in this task.
tasks.still_hard: Reconciling views, tolerances and actual assembly constraints.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise an inconsistent dimension or an unsafe assumption before fabrication.
tasks.altitude: The boilermaker retains drawing interpretation responsibility.

evidence.claim: Reading assembly relationships is skilled interpretation; no local labour saving is established.

assumptions: Boundary is studying released blueprints, excluding drawing production, material ordering and fabrication.
No machine-generated dimensions or structured safe-to-build flags are introduced. Drawing discrepancies remain subject to the existing clarification process.
Test available native drawing-viewer features before considering any extension; existing viewing runtime earns no labour saving.
Zero incremental upkeep because no new system or workflow is proposed.
research_questions: Is document retrieval a separately measured problem distinct from interpreting the drawing?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100, upkeep=0, net=0. Drawing interpretation stays fully human.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Rig heavy boiler sections and signal lifting operators

steps.what: Attach rigging to heavy frame and plate sections for the lift
Signal crane or hoist operators while positioning the lifted section

tasks.design: Keep physical rigging and real-time lift signalling with the authorised workers. Supporting lifting instructions may remain in {DOCS}; no software action replaces attachment, observation or communication during the lift.
tasks.previous_blocker: Safe lifting depends on physical conditions and continuous situational awareness.
tasks.enabler_now: No demonstrated software change removes this physical and signalling work.
tasks.still_hard: Changing clearances, load behaviour and communication under site conditions.
tasks.human_edge: Stop a lift when conditions no longer match the plan.
tasks.altitude: The boilermaker's lifting duties remain unchanged.

reach.learn: Required rigging qualifications and local signalling procedures

evidence.claim: Physical rigging and lift signalling remain manual work in this scenario.

assumptions: Boundary includes only the boilermaker's rigging and signalling effort; crane operator labour and lifting-plan production are separate and unchanged.
No automatic rigging approval, load classification or machine-issued crane commands are introduced. Existing human lifting procedures continue.
Native access to lifting documents can continue without a new system or runtime-saving claim.
Zero incremental upkeep because no workflow change is proposed.
unknowns: Required qualifications and site lifting arrangements
Actual split between rigging and signalling
research_questions: Is there a separate document-access delay that can be addressed without reducing required lifting work?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=55+45=100, upkeep=0, net=0. Physical rigging and real-time signalling remain human.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Blueprint judgement and physical lifting duties retain their full human time.
reach: Assist section positioning within required qualifications
role.ambitious_version: A skilled boilermaker with dependable drawings and protected attention during physical assembly and lifting.
